prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry: thresholds, connection/gate/towing/stand rules, border states, CTT tolerance, swap precedence/equity/customs eligibility/min notification/prohibited trades. Modes (ADM declares): Normal; Adverse Weather(shorter sweeps); Capacity Reduction State(binding metering; RFM may suspend swaps); Recovery Phase(RFM exits; preserves operator logic); Contingency Fallback(Contingency Operations Console); Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms). Actors: RFM=Regional Flow Manager(resolves swap disputes; reviews constraints changing rate/taxi-out/demand plan; confirms revised AAR); Airspace Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison; Tower Supervisor(stand readiness; rejects unsafe swaps; uses Runway Lighting Outage Card before approving Ironleaf status); ADM=Airport Duty Manager(Medical Diversion Notice, Customs Hold Release Note; checks sweep note vs swaps; ensures service reductions entered promptly, consistent with local procedures); Ramp Control Lead(Apron Sweep Completion Note; Ramp Movement Board gets swaps and infrastructure status); Ground Handling Dispatcher(Towbar Shortage Report; Handling Resource Planner); Aircraft Operator Rep(Crew Duty Extension Log; swap concurrence in Foxglove); Airline Operations Coordinator(revised TOBT; enters swap); Slot Coordinator(Slot Swap Permission Email after governance checks); NOL=Network Operations Liaison; System Support Engineer(investigates submission/validation/publication failures; no decision change unless authorized); Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator; MBO=Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward. Parts: Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform(records infrastructure events as constraints: effective time, duration, resource, confidence, approving authority); Airline Interface Adapter; Sector Load Monitor; Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service(recalculates demand vs constrained capacity); CAM=Capacity Assessment Module(AAR; Arrival Regulation Console applies revised AAR; compares event vs Airport Capacity Plan+weather; lighting limits→runway configuration constraint); Weather Ingest Gateway; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; GDP; Pushback Window Token; swaps; uses reduced capacity, fairness); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(TOBT; Collaborative Decision Log; Identity Access Service; presents infrastructure events; customs block); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager, displays constraints; updates metering

New part:
S704: The Common Situation Display shows the affected resource, start time, review time, and current decision status using language that can be understood by operational staff.
S705: The Alert Distribution Hub sends notifications when the constraint is created, materially changed, suspended, or cancelled.
S706: The Business Rules Registry defines which infrastructure events require approval, which events may be published as advisory information, and which events automatically trigger a Capacity Reduction State.
S707: During Adverse Weather Mode, lighting and navigation service limits are assessed together with ceiling, visibility, wind, and runway surface conditions before capacity values are released.
S708: During a Capacity Reduction State, the Regional Flow Platform maintains the infrastructure event as a controlling assumption until an authorized actor closes or supersedes it.
S709: The Collaborative Decision Log records the time of publication, approving role, capacity effect, affected services, and any later amendment made during the operating period.
S710: The Audit Event Ledger preserves the technical record of submission, validation, publication, acknowledgement, and withdrawal for accountability and post-event review.
S711: The Data Governance Steward monitors data quality for infrastructure events, including duplicate reports, inconsistent effective times, and unclear service descriptions.
S712: The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses completed infrastructure events to measure delay attribution, capacity recovery time, and the accuracy of initial duration estimates.
S713: When normal capability is restored, the Airport Duty Manager confirms closure in the Airport CDM Portal and the Regional Flow Platform returns the affected resource to Normal Operations or Recovery Phase handling as appropriate.
S714: Contingency operations cover any period in which the Regional Flow Platform cannot provide trusted automation for one or more airport, runway, apron, or airspace flow functions.
S715: A degraded operation is declared when data latency, service unavailability, or inconsistent operational outputs prevent users from relying on the normal decision support path without additional verification.
S716: The Airport Duty Manager is accountable for declaring the Contingency Fallback State after consultation with the Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, and System Support Engineer.
S717: The declaration identifies the affected functions, the operational area, the expected duration, and the authority that will approve restoration to Normal Operations or Recovery Phase.
S718: For voice coordination, the Contingency Operations Console is referred to as Silverpine during exercises and live fallback operation.
S719: The Contingency Operations Console provides a protected operating position with independent access to the Flight Data Exchange, Alert Distribution Hub, Audit Event Ledger, and Digital Briefing Room.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
